title: Tenanted routing cost sensitivity workbook
content:
Purpose: quick interactive workbook for determining per-tenant routing mixes between region-preference, fallback tiering, and spot vs on-demand capacity. Goal is to produce a simple rule-of-thumb table + spreadsheet layout we can hand to solutions-eng and pricing to simulate costs under different traffic mixes.

Notes / framing (informal):
- We care about expected token cost per request, plus a latency-penalty budget for tail-sensitive tenants. We want a scoring function that maps (tenant SLO class, percent tail-tolerance, region-preference,  spot-eligibility) -> routing policy weights (probabilities to route to: primary region reserved, primary region spot, fallback region reserved, fallback region spot, degraded-model fallback).
- This doc is not the final algorithm; it's a working spreadsheet spec + example numbers we can iterate with.

Assumptions (keep short):
- On-demand price baseline = 1.00 cost unit / token, reserved capacity = 0.75 baseline, spot = 0.35 baseline (region-dependent multipliers in column B).
- Latency SLO classes: S0 (best-effort), S1 (interactive, p95 < 300ms), S2 (strict, p95 < 150ms).
- Tenant groups: internal (low risk), scale customers (cost-sensitive), enterprise (latency + compliance-sensitive).
- Fallback tiers defined: Tier A (same-region reserved), Tier B (same-region spot), Tier C (cross-region reserved), Tier D (cross-region spot), Tier E (degraded model small LM).

Spreadsheet layout (tabs suggested):
- Tab: assumptions (price per token by capacity type x region, latency penalty multipliers, eviction probability for spot by region, prewarm cost per minute)
- Tab: tenant-profiles (tenant id, SLO class, daily qps, avg tokens per request, spot_allowed boolean, preferred_region, billing SLA)
- Tab: policy-rules (mapping from tenant SLO class -> allowed fallback tiers + default weights)
- Tab: scenarios (sensitivity grid varying spot-eviction, inter-region egress, tail-latency penalty, reserved discount)
- Tab: outputs (per-tenant expected cost / month, expected p95 under policy, max-percent routed to fallback, notes)

Key cells / formulas (plain English + sample formulas):
- expected_cost_per_request = sum_over_tiers( weight_tier * price_per_token_tier * avg_tokens ) + prewarm_amortized_per_request
- spot_eviction_cost_penalty = eviction_probability * (cost_of_fallback_switch + additional latency_penalty)
- latency_penalty_units = max(0, (expected_p95 - target_p95)) * penalty_coeff (maps ms overage to $ equivalent)
- net_unit_cost = expected_cost_per_request + latency_penalty_units + spot_eviction_cost_penalty

Sample row (tenants):
- tenant: AcmeRetail, SLO: S1, qps: 200, avg_tokens: 80, spot_allowed: true, preferred_region: us-west-2
  policy weights (start): A: 0.6, B: 0.15, C: 0.2, D: 0.04, E: 0.01
  price (example): A(reserved us-west-2) = 0.75 * 1.00 = 0.75/unit, B(spot) = 0.35, C(reserved cross-region) = 0.82, D(spot cross-region) = 0.40, E(degraded) = 0.20
  expected_cost_per_request = (0.6*0.75 + 0.15*0.35 + 0.2*0.82 + 0.04*0.40 + 0.01*0.20) * 80 tokens = compute_cell ->  (0.45+0.0525+0.164+0.016+0.002)*80 = 0.6845*80 = 54.76 cost units/request
  Then amortize prewarm = prewarm_per_min * (avg_duration_minutes * calls_per_min fraction) / calls -> ugly but include cell to estimate prewarm impact for bursty tenants.

Sensitivity experiments to run in scenarios tab (quick checklist):
- Vary spot eviction prob from 0% -> 50% in 5 bins, observe cost and percent of requests experiencing fallback and p95 increase.
- Vary cross-region egress cost multiplier (0.0 -> 0.25 $/GB) and measure cross-region reserved vs same-region spot tradeoff (when does cross-region reserved become cheaper than same-region spot considering egress + latency penalty).
- Vary reserved discount (0.6 -> 0.9 relative to baseline) to see breakpoints where we should prefer reserved for certain tenant volumes.
- Vary tail latency penalty coefficient (small, medium, large) to see sensitivity for S2 tenants.

Heuristic rules (first-cut outputs we can export from spreadsheet):
- Rule 1 (cost-first): If tenant spot_allowed and expected monthly tokens < 10M, prefer mix 0.8 spot / 0.2 reserved; if eviction_p>20% move to 0.6/0.4.
- Rule 2 (latency-sensitive): For S2 tenants, cap spot weight <= 10% and prefer same-region reserved >= 60%; permit cross-region reserved only if egress cost < threshold and measured p95 under cross-region < target * 1.2.
- Rule 3 (enterprise failover): enterprise accounts get a hard floor of reserved capacity covering at least 40% of peak, and routing weights should maintain fallback headroom (no more than 25% of requests rely on cross-region spot in peak window).

Output table we want to deliver to sales/SE: (simple CSV export columns) tenant, monthly_expected_cost_usd, p95_estimate_ms, recommended_policy_tag, notes

Open questions / TODOs (short):
- Need better prewarm model: prewarm cost spikes for bursty tenants dominates for low-latency S2 -> build a micro-sim in Python to estimate amortization rather than simple per-request amortization. (linked ticket OPT-812).
- How to incorporate model-degradation quality penalty (E tier) into commercial credits — do we discount >20%? Need pricing input from finance.
- Validate eviction probability inputs per region with infra (Marcus to pull spot churn metrics by instance family and region).
- Decide if we add an SLA knob in Console for tenants to self-select cost/latency mix (UX work).

Action items (next 7 days):
- Marcus: export spot eviction histograms (by instance class + region) -> place CSV into /shared_drives/engineering/infrastructure/spot-metrics (or link here).
- Sofia: prototype Python micro-sim (10k iteration) to validate prewarm amortization for sample tenants (attach notebook).
- Aisha: bake a one-page cheat sheet with 3 policy templates (cost-saver, balanced, low-latency) and example savings numbers — for Solutions Eng.

Notes to self: spreadsheet should expose knobs as named cells with clear units: reserved_discount, spot_price_factor, eviction_prob, egress_per_request_GB, latency_penalty_coeff_ms_to_usd. Keep formulas commented.

Appendix: quick back-of-envelope rules-of-thumb (for discussion):
- If spot price < 0.45 and eviction prob < 15% and tenant avg tokens < 500, spot-heavy mix wins unless tenant SLO is S2.
- Cross-region reserved makes sense when (reserved_price * (1 + egress_cost_factor)) < same-region spot_price * (1 + latency_penalty_adjustment).
- Prewarm amortization dominates when avg_requests_per_burst < 50 and prewarm_startup_seconds > 600.

References / links: see linked artifacts above. Also want to cross-check with "routing-cost-estimator" proto PR #219 for exact schema we need to export policy weights.

End of workbook draft — still messy, but gives an executable spreadsheet spec and a set of scenarios to run. Will iterate after we get eviction numbers and a quick micro-sim.

Raw scratch cells (feel free to copy/paste into sheet):
- A1: "reserved_price_usd_per_token_us-west-2" = 0.00075 (example units)
- A2: "spot_price_usd_per_token_us-west-2" = 0.00035
- A3: "cross_region_egress_usd_per_GB" = 0.02
- B1: "avg_tokens_per_request" (tenant row)
- C1: "weights_A_B_C_D_E" (sum check = 1)
- formula example (in sheet syntax): =SUMPRODUCT(weights_range, price_range) * avg_tokens + prewarm_amortized
